label: TP
reason: Three CodeQL alerts were assessed. Alert 1 (java/xss): User input from getParameter() flows through str to encodeForHTML() then to PrintWriter.println() - while ESAPI encoding is applied, the sink expression includes the encoded user data making this a real XSS pattern. Alert 2 (http-response-splitting): User input flows to cookie value which is added to response - potential for CRLF injection. Alert 3 (insecure-cookie): Cookie explicitly sets secure=false allowing transmission over non-HTTPS connections. All three alerts identify legitimate vulnerabilities in the code.

evidence.note: User parameter flows through str to HTML output via encodeForHTML() - XSS vulnerability
Cookie created from user input without secure flag - response splitting and insecure cookie vulnerabilities
